indication: ** 68-year-old female presenting with worsening dysphagia. Evaluate for esophageal lesion.
technique: ** Axial CT images were acquired from the thoracic inlet through the upper abdomen following the administration of intravenous contrast. Multiplanar reformats were performed.
findings:
**
The lungs are clear without any focal consolidation, suspicious pulmonary nodules, or masses. There is no evidence of pleural effusion or pneumothorax. The tracheobronchial tree is patent throughout.
Regarding the mediastinum, there is focal, circumferential wall thickening involving the distal oesophagus. This thickening appears relatively symmetric but results in a narrowing of the luminal diameter. No discrete eccentric mass is identified, though the wall is significantly thickened compared to the proximal segment. There is no evidence of mediastinal lymphadenopathy; the hilar and mediastinal lymph node stations are within normal limits for size.
The heart is normal in size. The pericardium is thin and unremarkable. The thoracic aorta and great vessels demonstrate normal caliber and course.
Incidental findings include mild atherosclerotic calcifications along the aortic arch. There are small, stable degenerative changes noted in the visualized thoracic vertebrae. A few tiny, non-specific calcified granulomas are seen in the right lower lobe, likely sequelae of prior healed infection.
The visualized portions of the upper abdomen, including the liver and adrenal glands, appear unremarkable.
conclusion:
**
Focal thickening of the distal oesophageal wall, suspicious for malignancy. No associated mediastinal lymphadenopathy or distant metastatic disease identified within the chest.
